author: furre-dev
body:
# DataStory Frontend Test

This PR is my solution to the DataStory Frontend Test. It's a Next.js 15 application focused on presenting country-based data, including dynamic and animated bar chart visualizations. The project uses modern React (including server components and async data fetching), TypeScript, Ant Design for UI, and Recharts for charting.

---

## What I Implemented and Why

- **Server-side Data Fetching:**  
  Leveraged Next.js [server functions](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/data-fetching/server-actions) and server components to fetch data at the server layer for better performance and simpler asynchronous logic. This also helps with SEO and initial load times.

- **Bar Chart Visualization (Recharts):**  
  Used [Recharts](https://recharts.org/) for dynamic, animated bar charts representing country-specific data in the `DataChart` component. Recharts allowed me to quickly ship something clean and functional.

- **Modern UI/UX:**  
  Used Ant Design and TailwindCSS to provide a visually appealing, responsive, and accessible UI.  
  Added multi-step selection (country, then measure) with clear feedback.

- **Component Structure:**  
  Broke down components into [atomic design](https://github.com/okasi/atomic-design) (see `/components/`).

- **Error and Loading States:**  
  Added basic error and loading screens using dedicated components (`ErrorPage`, `LoadingPage`).

- **TypeScript Everywhere:**  
  Used strong typing for all data structures and props.

- **Responsive Design:**  
  UI adapts across breakpoints and works on mobile screens.

- **GraphQL & Codegen:**  
  Data comes from a GraphQL endpoint. Used GraphQL codegen for safer types and development experience.


---

## What I Chose Not to Implement

- **In-depth Error Handling:**  
  Error handling is minimal, just displaying an error page––did not integrate advanced reporting/logging.

- **Custom Charting Library:**  
  Used Recharts instead of building a custom chart/bar visualization from scratch, to optimize for speed within the limited timeframe.

- **Scalability Patterns:**  
  Did not implement large-scale patterns due to time constraints and limited scope.

- **Performance Optimization:**  
  Did not deeply optimize re-renders (ex. memo), dynamic chart rendering and animation performance for large data sets or older devices.

- **Testing:**  
  No unit/integration/E2E tests included.

---

## Scores & Focus Breakdown (for my 2-hour timeframe)

- **UX/UI:** 8/10  
  Focused on clean, clear interactions and design for a smooth user experience.

- **Performance:** 6/10  
  Fetches done server-side for a fast initial load, but client performance around component re-renders could be much better.

- **Scalability:** 5/10  
  App is split into reusable components, but would need better structure for a large project.

- **Error Handling:** 1/10  
  Only basic error UI and logging.

- **Testing:** 0/10  
  Simply had no time.

---

## What I'd Do Next With More Time

- **URL Select Pre-fill:**  
  I did not have time to implement the feature where, if a country or measure already exist in the URL, the selects would auto-select the correct option to reflect that. This is a feature I really wanted to include for better deep-linking UX.

- **Scalability & Robustness:**  
  Refactor the codebase to make it even easier to expand—especially so new "measurements" or "inputs" (for example, new types of data to visualize) can be added smoothly, with no code duplication or structural constraints. I want the architecture to support truly rapid addition of new features, so the system grows gracefully as requirements change. This may include introducing context or state management, and further modularizing the relevant data flow and UI logic.

- **Fix inconsistent naming (e.g., some variables/props are called "mesure" while others are "measure"):**  
  In the interest of delivering a working solution within the 2-hour window, I prioritized progress over polish. As a result, some inconsistencies slipped through—like the varying spelling of "measure." With more time, I'd refactor for consistency and overall code quality while maintaining robustness.

- **Deeper Performance Improvements:**  
  Optimize rendering, especially for larger data and on slower devices.

- **Stronger Error Handling:**  
  Add robust error tracking and user feedback (e.g. Sentry integration, granular error boundaries).

- **Custom Chart Component:**  
  Instead of Recharts, I’d LOVE to create a custom bar chart tailored for this project, both for creativity and better fine-tuned performance/UI. I enjoy building creative UI components from the ground up, and it's also important to me that my product looks "original" and not like every other data website.

- **End-to-end & Unit Testing:**  
  Add meaningful tests to catch regressions and document user flows.

- **Better Accessibility:**  
  Ensure full keyboard and screen reader navigation, polish contrast and ARIA as needed.

- **Advanced Features:**  
  CSV export/download, etc.

- **More Metrics & Insights:**  
  Add richer analytical features, like ranking the current country compared to others, or surfacing useful insights (for example, detecting periods where wars or major events caused significant changes in the population).


---

## Decisions & Trade-offs

- **Server-side Functions**:  
  Shifted data fetching to the server to improve perceived performance and simplify maintainability in the Next.js app.

- **Limited Error Handling**:  
  Opted for prioritizing smooth data flow and user experience over comprehensive error handling for the initial phase.

- **Time Management**:  
  Focused on optimizing the user journey and providing clear visual feedback, rather than investing time in code extensibility or deep performance optimizations.

- **State Management**:  
  Managed country and measure states through the URL, replacing the use of `useState` for better persistence and sharing of state across sessions.

---

author: penelopeysm
body:
In Turing.jl v0.37, when a Gibbs sampler is used without specifying component samplers for all variables, the variables without samplers are sampled once at the beginning and don't ever move from there. See https://github.com/TuringLang/Turing.jl/issues/2536.

This patch is required to preserve that behaviour - without this patch it will throw a MethodError as it was trying to look for the newly added method. Specifically it was this line in Turing.jl that was calling the missing method https://github.com/TuringLang/Turing.jl/blob/fc32e10bc17ae3fda4d7e825b6fde45dc7bdb179/src/mcmc/gibbs.jl#L162-L168

Should hopefully be simple enough to approve -- though I'm very much not a fan of how the N optional arguments force us to define 2^N methods, and it may be worth thinking about how to deal with this in a better way long-term. See also #720.

author: x-infin1ty-x
body:
Enabling Support for Conditional Multi-Part Upload (#18093)

At a Glance:
Implement both synchronous and asynchronous conditional-upload methods in S3BlobContainer, backed by logical functions in AsyncTransferManager

Method | Location | Purpose/Functionality -- | -- | -- executeMultipartUploadConditionally | S3BlobContainer | Conditional multipart upload (sync) asyncBlobUploadConditionally | S3BlobContainer | Conditional streamed upload (async) uploadObjectConditionally | AsyncTransferManager | Core async conditional upload implementation Helpers in AsyncTransferManager |   | uploadInOneChunkConditionally Helpers in AsyncTransferManager |   | uploadInPartsConditionally Helpers in AsyncTransferManager |   | doUploadInPartsConditionally Helpers in AsyncTransferManager |   | handleConditionalException

Summary of Changes

  • Add executeMultipartUploadConditionally(...) to S3BlobContainer

  • Add asyncBlobUploadConditionally(...) to S3BlobContainer

  • Implement uploadObjectConditionally(...) in AsyncTransferManager

  • Introduce helper routines: uploadInOneChunkConditionally, uploadInPartsConditionally, doUploadInPartsConditionally, and handleConditionalException

  • Define ConditionalWriteOptions to express “If-Match” and “If-None-Match” conditions

  • Define ConditionalWriteResponse to wrap returned ETag or propagate failures

  • Extend tests to cover conditional success, precondition failures, data integrity, and size boundaries

Core Workflow

  1. Validate part size (≥ 5 MB) and total upload size (≤ 5 TB).

  2. Initialize upload by creating a multipart request with bucket, key, ACL, storage class, metadata, and SSE (AES256 or KMS).

  3. Transfer Data

    • Sync: iterate parts sequentially using AWS SDK, buffering if retries are enabled.

    • Async: delegate to AsyncTransferManager.uploadObjectConditionally, which chooses single-chunk or multipart flow via its helper methods.

  4. Complete Conditionally by setting either If-Match or If-None-Match: * on the complete-upload request based on ConditionalWriteOptions.

  5. Respond with ConditionalWriteResponse.success(etag) on success or translate failures:

    • HTTP 412 → OpenSearchException("stale_primary_shard") + abort multipart.

    • Other errors → IOException (sync) or failed CompletableFuture/listener (async) + abort if uploadId exists.

    • Abort failures are logged but do not mask the original exception.

Test Coverage

executeMultipartUploadConditionally Test Suite

  • testExecuteMultipartUploadConditionallyWithEtagMatchSuccess

  • testExecuteMultipartUploadConditionallyWithMetadataAndSSE

  • testExecuteMultipartUploadConditionallyContentIntegrity

  • testExecuteMultipartUploadConditionallySizeValidation

  • testExecuteMultipartUploadConditionallyPreconditionFailed

AsyncTransferManager Conditional Upload Tests

  • testConditionalOneChunkUpload

  • testConditionalOneChunkUploadPreconditionFailed

  • testConditionalOneChunkUploadCorruption

  • testConditionalMultipartUploadPreconditionFailed

  • testConditionalMultipartUploadCorruption

Container-Level and Retry Tests

  • testFailureWhenLargeFileRedirectedConditional

  • testLargeFileRedirectedConditional

  • testLargeFileRedirectedConditionalPreconditionFailed

  • testLargeFileRedirectedConditionalConflict

  • testWriteBlobByStreamsConditionalFailure

--- ### Related Issue Concerned RFC : [RFC #17763](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/issues/17763) Parent Meta Issue : [Meta #17859](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/issues/17859) By submitting this pull request, I confirm that my contribution is made under the terms of the Apache 2.0 license. For more information on following Developer Certificate of Origin and signing off your commits, please check [here](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#developer-certificate-of-origin). ### Flow Diagram for executeMultipartUploadConditionally: ![Mermaid Chart - Create complex, visual diagrams with text A smarter way of creating diagrams -2025-05-29-085837](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94efdf1b-493e-4c31-8a35-2dc34feda5f9)

author: susumutomita
body:
This pull request introduces significant changes to the blockchain application, focusing on improving modularity, simplifying commands, and enhancing code organization. The most notable updates include changes to the `docker-compose.yml` configuration, refactoring of blockchain core functionality, and restructuring of peer-to-peer communication logic.

### Configuration Updates:
* Updated `docker-compose.yml` commands to simplify node initialization by removing flag-based arguments and replacing them with positional parameters. For example, the `--listen` and `--connect` flags were replaced with direct arguments like `3000` or `3001 node1:3000` for better clarity and consistency. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e45e45baeda1c1e73482975a664062aa56f20c03dd9d64a827aba57775bed0d3L10-R10) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e45e45baeda1c1e73482975a664062aa56f20c03dd9d64a827aba57775bed0d3L19-R19) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-e45e45baeda1c1e73482975a664062aa56f20c03dd9d64a827aba57775bed0d3L28-R28)

### Blockchain Core Enhancements:
* Added comprehensive documentation for blockchain functions, such as `calculateHash`, `mineBlock`, and `verifyBlockPow`, to improve readability and maintainability. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-abd5e1fc144aa3d7609d47426bd001a5c9759d3bc118937e2473b7223aa7a6aaR1-R7) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-abd5e1fc144aa3d7609d47426bd001a5c9759d3bc118937e2473b7223aa7a6aaR16-R43) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-abd5e1fc144aa3d7609d47426bd001a5c9759d3bc118937e2473b7223aa7a6aaL37-R108)
* Made `chain_store` a `pub var` to allow external modules to access the blockchain state directly.
* Removed extensive test cases from `blockchain.zig` to streamline the file and focus on core functionality.

[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-abd5e1fc144aa3d7609d47426bd001a5c9759d3bc118937e2473b7223aa7a6aaL111-R174) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-afb086cbdc48682f21bcb14abfd5fb39689b1b4683936b55fea8d903da8e67d1L281-L505)

It also
### Enhancements to `kWaveGrid` Class:

* **New Factory Methods**:
  - Added `from_geometry` and `from_domain` class methods to simplify the creation of `kWaveGrid` instances based on physical domain dimensions, acoustic properties, and resolution requirements. These methods encapsulate grid spacing and size calculations.

* **Utility Properties**:
  - Introduced `x_max`, `y_max`, and `z_max` properties to provide easy access to the maximum extents of the grid in each dimension.


### Refactoring in Example Scripts:

* **Simplified Grid Initialization**:
  - Replaced manual grid size and spacing calculations with the new `kWaveGrid.from_domain` factory method in `at_circular_piston_3D.py` and `at_focused_bowl_3D.py`. This reduces redundant code and ensures consistency in grid creation. author: cjwatson
body: https://bugs.debian.org/1103066 reported test failures on Debian's i386 architecture.  After some digging I found that tests were hitting `ENOMEM` depending on which other tests had been run previously, suggesting test isolation problems; i386 has a more limited address space than most other architectures so is more likely to run into this sort of thing.  Forcing thread pools to be shut down between tests seems to avoid this problem.

author: lihaoyi
body:
Fixes https://github.com/com-lihaoyi/mill/issues/4971

With this PR, any top-level `object package` in a `build.mill` or `package.mill` file has the `extends RootModule` or `extends SubfolderModule` automatically inserted. 

Before this PR we were already over-writing the `extends RootModule` with the correct type, so this just makes it insert the correct type even when `extends RootModule` is not provided (although we still require that it extends some kind of `mill.Module`). 

If there is an existing `extends RootModule`, we accept that for now to ease in the migration

# 데이터베이스 연결 재시도 문제 해결 및 T_CONT_DADAM_FILE_MAP 테이블 처리 개선

데이터베이스가 이미 연결된 상태에서도 계속 재연결을 시도하는 문제를 해결하고, T_CONT_DADAM_FILE_MAP 테이블이 원격에 없을 경우 로컬에 생성하는 로직을 개선했습니다.

## 개선 내용

1. **연결 상태 확인과 연결 시도 로직 분리**
   - `checkConnectionStatus` 함수: 기존 연결 상태만 확인
   - `initializeConnections` 함수: 초기 연결 시도
   - `monitorConnections` 함수: 상태 확인만 수행

2. **불필요한 재연결 시도 방지**
   - 서버 시작 시 초기 연결만 시도
   - 이후 30초마다 상태 확인만 수행
   - 연결 상태 변경 시에만 로그 출력

3. **T_CONT_DADAM_FILE_MAP 테이블 처리 개선**
   - 원격 MySQL에 테이블 생성 권한이 없을 경우 로컬 SQLite에 생성
   - WebhardHash 모델의 로컬/원격 버전 모두 지원
   - 테이블 생성 실패 시 명확한 오류 메시지 출력

## 테스트 방법

서버 시작 시 로그를 확인하여 다음 사항을 확인할 수 있습니다:
- 초기 연결 시도 후 불필요한 재연결 시도가 없는지 확인
- T_CONT_DADAM_FILE_MAP 테이블 생성 권한 오류 발생 시 로컬 SQLite에 테이블이 생성되는지 확인
- 연결 상태 변경 시에만 로그가 출력되는지 확인

author: estruttijp
body:
### **Descrição:**  
Este PR implementa a versão atual da "Loja", nosso site de venda de serviços. A estrutura principal está concluída e pronta para revisão. Alguns pontos ainda precisam de melhorias, mas o estado atual é suficiente para seguir com o PR.

### **Principais mudanças:**  
✅ Desenvolvimento completo da interface da Loja  
✅ Implementação do fluxo de navegação e compra  
✅ Ajuste de estilos e responsividade  
✅ Correções de bugs menores na UI  

### **Pontos pendentes para ajustes futuros:**  
⚠ Dockerização incompleta – necessidade de ajustes na configuração  
⚠ Falta de testes automatizados – implementação pendente  
⚠ Melhorias de performance e otimização de código  

### **Como testar:**  
1. Faça checkout da branch `dev`:  
   ```bash
   git checkout dev
   ```
2. Rode a aplicação localmente:  
   ```bash
   docker-compose up
   ```
3. **Acessando o container e executando os comandos do Artisan**
Para configurar e executar tarefas essenciais da aplicação, é necessário entrar no container e rodar os seguintes comandos:

- Acesse o container de aplicação:
```bash
     docker-compose exec -it app    bash
```
- Dentro do container, execute:
```bash
     php artisan migrate
     php artisan db:seed
     php artisan queue:work
```
3. Teste os principais fluxos da Loja, incluindo cadastro, navegação e compra.  

### **Observações finais:**  
Este PR tem como objetivo levar a Loja para a `main`, garantindo que as funcionalidades essenciais estejam disponíveis. A parte de Docker e testes será adicionada posteriormente.

body:
This PR is to close issue #28 (Add Postgres Support)

✔️ Checklist

Adds support for interacting with PostgreSQL databases:
- [x] Inserting pandas/polars DataFrames directly into Postgres tables, with automatic table creation and batch inserts.
- [x] Flexible support for both psycopg2 and pg8000 DBAPI drivers.
- [x] Connection management, SQL execution, and error handling

Testing:
- [x] Unit tests using mocks for both DBAPI drivers.
- [x] Integration tested against a local Postgres instance.

ruby 3.2.8 (2025-03-26 revision 13f495dc2c) +YJIT [x86_64-linux]
Warming up --------------------------------------
          block call     1.296M i/100ms
   yield with &block     1.708M i/100ms
yield without &block     1.687M i/100ms
Calculating -------------------------------------
          block call     12.964M (± 0.8%) i/s   (77.14 ns/i) -     66.097M in   5.098814s
   yield with &block     17.186M (± 0.5%) i/s   (58.19 ns/i) -     87.092M in   5.067659s
yield without &block     17.162M (± 0.3%) i/s   (58.27 ns/i) -     86.062M in   5.014579s

Comparison:
   yield with &block: 17186340.4 i/s
yield without &block: 17162477.2 i/s - same-ish: difference falls within error
          block call: 12964086.6 i/s - 1.33x  slower
```

yield with/without &block is same-ish. For simplicity, use without &block.

Appendix: benchmark script

```ruby
require 'bundler/inline'
gemfile do
  source 'https://rubygems.org'
  gem 'benchmark-ips'
  gem 'benchmark-memory'
end

def block_call(s, &block)
  block.call(s) if block_given?
end

def yield_with_block(s, &block)
  yield(s) if block_given?
end

def yield_without_block(s)
  yield(s) if block_given?
end

Benchmark.ips do |x|
  x.report("block call") {
    block_call("dummy") do |message|
      message
    end
  }
  x.report("yield with &block") {
    yield_with_block("dummy") do |message|
      message
    end
  }
  x.report("yield without &block") {
    yield_without_block("dummy") do |message|
      message
    end
  }
  x.compare!
end
```

body:
### Changes 

- A new property `Headers` will now be exposed as part of the `AccessTokenResponse`.
- This property will contain all the raw headers returned as part of the http response.
- Extension methods on `Headers` property will allow users to parse the raw response headers into easily understandable models. (shown in `examples.md`)
- Augmented the `RateLimitException` with more details to distinguish if the rate limiting was due to token quota breach or was due to generic limiting rules set.

### References 📚 
- [SDK-5883](https://auth0team.atlassian.net/browse/SDK-5883)


### Testing
- Added unit and integration test cases for the newly added response header parsing, extension methods, rate-limit exception.

Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Babel has inefficient RegExp complexity in generated code with .replace when transpiling named capturing groups

Impact

When using Babel to compile regular expression named capturing groups, Babel will generate a polyfill for the .replace method that has quadratic complexity on some specific replacement pattern strings (i.e. the second argument passed to .replace).

Your generated code is vulnerable if all the following conditions are true:

  • You use Babel to compile regular expression named capturing groups
  • You use the .replace method on a regular expression that contains named capturing groups
  • Your code uses untrusted strings as the second argument of .replace

If you are using @babel/preset-env with the targets option, the transform that injects the vulnerable code is automatically enabled if:

  • you use duplicated named capturing groups, and target any browser older than Chrome/Edge 126, Opera 112, Firefox 129, Safari 17.4, or Node.js 23
  • you use any named capturing groups, and target any browser older than Chrome 64, Opera 71, Edge 79, Firefox 78, Safari 11.1, or Node.js 10

You can verify what transforms @babel/preset-env is using by enabling the debug option.

Patches

This problem has been fixed in @babel/helpers and @babel/runtime 7.26.10 and 8.0.0-alpha.17, please upgrade. It's likely that you do not directly depend on @babel/helpers, and instead you depend on @babel/core (which itself depends on @babel/helpers). Upgrading to @babel/core 7.26.10 is not required, but it guarantees that you are on a new enough @babel/helpers version.

Please note that just updating your Babel dependencies is not enough: you will also need to re-compile your code.

Workarounds

If you are passing user-provided strings as the second argument of .replace on regular expressions that contain named capturing groups, validate the input and make sure it does not contain the substring $< if it's then not followed by > (possibly with other characters in between).

References

This vulnerability was reported and fixed in #17173.

author: pedrodesanti
body:
Przinha que implementa um servico de comunicacao bluetooth
- Basicamente é bem parecido com o storage, eu fiz uma interface ISerialVariable que extende o ISerializable colocando coisas inportantes como nome do tipo da variavel, nome da variavel e id
- Tem duas classes que implementam essa interface, o CustomSerialVariable e o PrimitiveSerialVariable
- Tem um SerialVariablePool que vai adicionar referencias as varaivei em um mapa
- Um logger pra mandar mg de string
- Um CommunicationService que recebe um logger e um SerialVariablePool e automaticamente fica mandando ou recebendo essas variaveis (pelo bluetooth no nosso caso

A forma como o CommunicationService é basicamente assim:
- O cliente (webapp) vai se conectar no micras e mandar um request de mapa de variaveis, pra saber quais sao todas as variaveis que serão sincronizadas entre os dois, e as respectivas informacoes delas (id, nome, tipo da variavel)
- A partir dai o micras e o cliente apensa se comunicarão com uma msg que contem um id e um payload
- O cliente vai mandar para o micras as variaveis write_only e o micras vai desserializar o conteudo delas encaminhando para a variavel com id certo
- O micras vai ficar mandando todas as variáveis read_only pro cliente

To address the issue, we will add a rate limiter specifically for the `GET /` route. This will limit the number of requests an IP address can make to this endpoint within a specified time window. We will use the `express-rate-limit` package, which is already imported in the file. The rate limiter will be configured to allow a maximum of 100 requests per 15 minutes, consistent with the existing rate limiters in the codebase.

Steps:
1. Define a new rate limiter (`getUsersLimiter`) for the `GET /` route.
2. Apply the rate limiter as middleware to the route.

author: abbari6
body:
### Overview:
This PR introduces the following features and improvements:

1. **Refresh Token Functionality**: 
   - Added a new strategy for refreshing user tokens to extend the user's session.
   - Implemented a new `RefreshTokenStrategy` for handling token renewal using refresh tokens.

2. **Rate-Limiting and Caching**:
   - Introduced Redis caching to manage rate-limiting instead of in-memory storage. This provides more scalability and persistence.
   - Modified `RateLimitGuard` to support Redis for storing rate-limiting data, enhancing the guard's performance and reliability.
   - Integrated `CacheService` for handling Redis interactions, including setting, getting, deleting cache values, and managing TTL (Time To Live).

3. **Guard Instantiation Fix**:
   - Fixed the instantiation of `RateLimitGuard` by manually passing the `CacheService` and `Reflector` dependencies in `main.ts` to ensure proper guard functionality.

### How it Works:
- **Rate-Limiting**: The `RateLimitGuard` now uses Redis to store and manage the rate-limiting data (e.g., request count, expiration time) for each user or IP, ensuring that rate limits are applied consistently.
- **Refresh Tokens**: A new refresh token mechanism has been added to the authentication flow, allowing users to refresh their session without re-authenticating.
- **Cache Service**: The `CacheService` utilizes Redis for cache management, including handling TTL to ensure keys are automatically deleted after expiration.

### Testing:
- The implementation has been tested locally and works as expected with Redis integration.
- Rate-limiting behavior and refresh token flow have been validated.

author: mernen
body:
The main goal here is to allow revset completion in more complex expressions — for example, being able to type `jj log -r first-bookmark..secon`<TAB> and getting `second-bookmark` filled in. It will also work for significantly more complex expressions, with a few important caveats:

- `foo::bar` and `all:foo` won't work in Bash by default, due to `$COMP_WORDBREAKS` including `:`. The recommended solution is apparently to consider this a mistake and remove it globally in your `.bashrc`:

      COMP_WORDBREAKS=${COMP_WORDBREAKS//:}

  (or you can just run it in your current shell to try it.) This can, however, be worked around at the completion script, and I'll see if the `clap` folks are interested in building the workaround into `clap_complete`. It works out of the box in fish and zsh, though.
- Expressions prefixed with quotes generally do not work. I'll propose some improvements to `clap_complete` for Bash, but I'm not familiar with other shells.

body:
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:
1. Make sure to read the Contributing Guide before submitting your PR: https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
2. If this PR closes another issue, add 'closes #<issue number>' somewhere in the PR summary. GitHub will automatically close that issue when this PR gets merged. Alternatively, adding 'refs #<issue number>' will not close the issue, but help provide the reviewer more context.-->

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Implement Helm client and SDK changes to support Server Side Apply.

Notably, this PR does:
1. Creates the `--service-side` and `--force-conflicts` flags (and corresponding API objects), and passes these to Kubernetes client
2. Creates an `ApplyMethod` field in release, which tracks the apply method (client or server side) used to deploy the chart
    - Upon upgrade, the next release will default to that apply method (unless override by e.g. CLI flag)
    - Prints this field in `helm get metadata`
3. When upgrade a previous chart release that utilized client-side apply, Kubernetes field management objects are converted/upgrade to server-side management.

**Special notes for your reviewer**:
Specification documented in: [HIP-0023](https://github.com/helm/community/blob/main/hips/hip-0023.md)

The Kubernetes client changes were done in: https://github.com/helm/helm/pull/31030

- [x] this PR contains user facing changes (the `docs needed` label should be applied if so)
- [x] this PR contains unit tests
- [x] this PR has been tested for backwards compatibility

body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16d0da99-d6b4-434d-b8e6-56d70559a46e

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1f0b499a-5f01-4bfd-be58-5d32bc7ba34b

I updated more of the code than I intended, but we should be good to go for this release! I'll wait to publish the release until the next series of server and monthly updates finish in case of any dependency updates.

I spent more time in this PR testing the Universal Links since I never added the confirmation messages after performing various profile actions. The [tech notes](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3155-debugging-universal-links) were a good resource to learn about all the different ways to test and debug these links. (I'm gonna refer to these as deep links from here on out since it's quicker to type. :P) For example, I can paste the deep link in Notes or Reminders and check if it opens the app instead of Safari. Or I can long-press it to explicitly choose to open one or the other. I can also test the deep link in the Developer Settings with a message explaining if it's not implemented properly.  On the Mac, I can run `swcutil` to check if the Apple App Site Association file is set up properly in the website. Below are some of the results (aasa.json refers to the app site file in [ez-recipes-web](https://github.com/Abhiek187/ez-recipes-web/blob/main/src/.well-known/apple-app-site-association)):

```bash
$ sudo swcutil verify -d ez-recipes-web.onrender.com -j aasa.json

Service:              applinks
App ID:               UF6E5BVT98.com.abhiek.EZ-Recipes
Domain:               ez-recipes-web.onrender.com
User Approval:        unspecified
Site/Fmwk Approval:   unspecified
Flags:                
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Service:              webcredentials
App ID:               UF6E5BVT98.com.abhiek.EZ-Recipes
Domain:               ez-recipes-web.onrender.com
User Approval:        unspecified
Site/Fmwk Approval:   unspecified
Flags:
```

```bash
$ sudo swcutil verify -d ez-recipes-web.onrender.com -j aasa.json -u "https://ez-recipes-web.onrender.com/recipe/644783"
{ s = applinks, a = UF6E5BVT98.com.abhiek.EZ-Recipes, d = ez-recipes-web.onrender.com }: Pattern "https://ez-recipes-web.onrender.com/recipe/644783" matched.
{ s = webcredentials, a = UF6E5BVT98.com.abhiek.EZ-Recipes, d = ez-recipes-web.onrender.com }: Pattern "https://ez-recipes-web.onrender.com/recipe/644783" matched.
```

```bash
$ sudo swcutil verify -d ez-recipes-web.onrender.com -j aasa.json -u "https://ez-recipes-web.onrender.com/profile?action=verifyEmail"
{ s = applinks, a = UF6E5BVT98.com.abhiek.EZ-Recipes, d = ez-recipes-web.onrender.com }: Pattern "https://ez-recipes-web.onrender.com/profile?action=verifyEmail" matched.
{ s = webcredentials, a = UF6E5BVT98.com.abhiek.EZ-Recipes, d = ez-recipes-web.onrender.com }: Pattern "https://ez-recipes-web.onrender.com/profile?action=verifyEmail" matched.
```

Even though I have the app installed locally, since I can't sign it using the entitlements, the deep link won't work. However, I can still force the app to run the same closure on launch as if was opened via a URL. I used the same test URLs from the Android app and the results are shown in the demos above.

The app works well on small devices, but I made a few adjustments to improve the design on iPads. First, I removed the secondary view on the home screen to make more room for the accordions. I could open them by default, but I didn't want to load all those recipes on launch since that would eat up the server's quota. Second, I adjusted the spacing of a few elements on the recipe screen so they're not so far apart on wide screens. I also fixed the form error animation to fade whenever it disappears so it doesn't overlap with other elements, which ended up being a simple fix.

The screenshot requirements have changed since the last release. We only need the largest-sized iPhone and iPad, and the App Store will automatically scale down the screenshots for smaller devices. Unfortunately, Fastlane has been struggling to keep up-to-date with the latest devices. Newer devices won't show up in the HTML preview, but the screenshots are still saved at least to disk. Device frames aren't available for iPhone 15 or 16. I still like having them in the README, so I continued using the iPhone 14 Pro Max to take screenshots. I did take these manually since Fastlane seems to struggle with finding simulators on specific patch iOS versions. In my case, I wanted to take screenshots on an iPhone SE, but they're only available on iOS 18.3.1 or earlier. By default, Fastlane will check for 18.4 (the latest version as of this writing). If I specify 18.3.1 in the Snapfile, it will try searching for 18.3 and fail. ☹️ Also, I had to remove Mac Catalyst as a supported destination for unit & UI tests since Fastlane will only select the Mac if it's available, instead of the devices I specified. Apparently, that bug has been there for a year now, but I might've encountered it now since I switched to an Apple chip.

author: chireddy
body:
This PR adds GitHub Actions workflows for CI/CD pipeline:

## Main CI/CD Pipeline (ci-cd.yml)
- Builds the Java application with Maven
- Runs tests
- Builds and pushes Docker image (when merged to main/master)
- **Interactive approval process** with comments and resume capability
- Deployment steps after approval

## Build Verification (build-verification.yml)
- Simple workflow to verify builds on PRs without requiring Docker credentials

## Resume Deployment (resume-deployment.yml)
- Allows resuming a deployment after rejection with comments
- Provides options to approve or continue rejection
- Maintains approval history

Also adds a README with detailed instructions for using the pipeline.

### Required Setup
- DOCKER_USERNAME: Docker Hub username
- DOCKER_PASSWORD: Docker Hub password or access token
- GitHub environment named `production-approval` with required reviewers

author: shalinib-ibm
body:
This patch upstreams llamafile's cpu matrix multiplication kernels for ppc64le using MMA builtins for BF16 data type.

This change results in 9x - 40x gains
in total speed S t/s (ie all tokens/total time), across various batch sizes tested using llama-batched-bench benchmark.

The patch is tested with Meta-Lllama-3-8B,
and Mistral-7B models (BF16 models generated by using llama-quantize from corresponding FP32 models) on an IBM POWER10 machine.

*Make sure to read the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) before submitting a PR*

author: ampandey-amd
body:
AMDGPU target runtimes(offload,hip,flang_rt) are dependent on host shared library 'libclang_rt.asan-x86_64.so' when ASan instrumentation is enabled. 'LLVM_ENABLE_PER_TARGET_RUNTIME_DIR' is by default on when runtimes are enabled using 'LLVM_ENABLE_RUNTIMES'. The runtimes can be build using 'LLVM_ENABLE_PROJECTS' or there can be mix usage of enabling runtimes via both LLVM_ENABLE_PROJECTS or LLVM_ENABLE_RUNTIMES. This patch fixes the searching of asan shared library and removing any dependency on runtimes build with/without
'LLVM_ENABLE_PER_TARGET_RUNTIME_DIR'.

author: arvi18
body:
I have tried to spare users a long debugging session searching for a .bazelrc
line that was not applied.

The main issue is in the client parser, which assumes that the first word on a line is _always_ a command. If you are unlucky enough, you forgot the command an passed a single flag. The client assumes it is a command with no flags, and passes nothing to the server, hence silently ignoring the bogus line.

I have changed the client to refuse lines with a single word, which is both simpler to do, and prevents what seems like a code smell anyway.

It is thus a breaking change for users who used to comment only the flag and not the command, or those who have empty commands to keep blocks together.
Overall, the RC files lack a proper specification, which makes it impossible to know precisely what is valid.

```
# The two following lines will no more work.
common # --host_jvm_args=-Xmx1024m
common
```

The second commit is optional. It turns a warning about unrecognized command names into an error.
I think it makes sense to address these issues early. It may break users config if commands are removed in the future, but that set is pretty stable now.

Fixes #15245

author: haritha-koloth
body:
## Description
This PR implements connector-side support for join pushdown in JDBC connectors, leveraging the foundational changes introduced in [24115](https://github.com/prestodb/presto/pull/24115). The changes enable JDBC connectors to perform join pushdown by rebuilding the query to execute joins directly on the remote datasource.

## Motivation and Context
Fixes [23152](https://github.com/prestodb/presto/issues/23152)

## Impact
This update includes the connector-side changes required to enable join pushdown in JDBC connectors, building on the foundational SPI and core changes introduced earlier. 

Detailed RFC - https://github.com/prestodb/rfcs/pull/32

## Test Plan
Unit tests added for newly added logic

## Contributor checklist

- [ ] Please make sure your submission complies with our [contributing guide](https://github.com/prestodb/presto/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md), in particular [code style](https://github.com/prestodb/presto/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-style) and [commit standards](https://github.com/prestodb/presto/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#commit-standards).
- [ ] PR description addresses the issue accurately and concisely.  If the change is non-trivial, a GitHub Issue is referenced.
- [ ] Documented new properties (with its default value), SQL syntax, functions, or other functionality.
- [ ] If release notes are required, they follow the [release notes guidelines](https://github.com/prestodb/presto/wiki/Release-Notes-Guidelines).
- [ ] Adequate tests were added if applicable.
- [ ] CI passed.

## Release Notes
Please follow [release notes guidelines](https://github.com/prestodb/presto/wiki/Release-Notes-Guidelines) and fill in the release notes below.

```
== RELEASE NOTES ==
JDBC Driver Changes
* Add ``catalog.partial-predicate-push-down`` configuration property and ``partial_predicate_push_down`` session property. Applicable only to JDBC connectors.
When set to ``true`` these properties enable partial predicate pushdown to the underlying data source. Enable this property for join pushdown to be effective with JDBC connectors.

```

author: sorrymakershen
body:
[Feature] Require at least one uppercase letter in passwords

This commit implements enhanced password security measures by requiring at least one uppercase letter in user passwords. Changes include:

- Server-side validation in user registration and profile update routes
- Client-side validation in JavaScript for better user experience
- Clear user feedback messages about the new password requirement
- Updated form templates with helpful password requirement hints

These changes improve the overall security posture of the application by enforcing stronger password complexity requirements, reducing the risk of brute force attacks.

author: ethanndickson
body:
Closes https://github.com/coder/vscode-coder/issues/447
Closes https://github.com/coder/jetbrains-coder/issues/543
Closes https://github.com/coder/coder-jetbrains-toolbox/issues/21

This PR adds Coder Connect support to `coder ssh --stdio`. 

When connecting to a workspace, if `--force-new-tunnel` is not passed, the CLI will first do a DNS lookup for `<agent>.<workspace>.<owner>.<hostname-suffix>`. If an IP address is returned, and it's within the Coder service prefix, the CLI will not create a new tailnet connection to the workspace, and instead dial the SSH server running on port 22 on the workspace directly over TCP.

This allows IDE extensions to use the Coder Connect tunnel, without requiring any modifications to the extensions themselves. 

Additionally, `using_coder_connect` is added to the `sshNetworkStats` file, which the VS Code extension (and maybe Jetbrains?) will be able to read, and indicate to the user that they are using Coder Connect.

One advantage of this approach is that running `coder ssh --stdio` on an offline workspace with Coder Connect enabled will have the CLI wait for the workspace to build, the agent to connect (and optionally, for the startup scripts to finish), before finally connecting using the Coder Connect tunnel.

As a result, `coder ssh --stdio` has the overhead of looking up the workspace and agent, and checking if they are running. On my device, this meant `coder ssh --stdio <workspace>` was approximately a second slower than just connecting to the workspace directly using `ssh <workspace>.coder` (I would assume anyone serious about their Coder Connect usage would know to just do the latter anyway).
 
To ensure this doesn't come at a significant performance cost, I've also benchmarked this PR.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark</summary>

## Methodology
All tests were completed on `dev.coder.com`, where a Linux workspace running in AWS `us-west1` was created.
The machine running Coder Desktop (the 'client') was a Windows VM running in the same AWS region and VPC as the workspace.

To test the performance of specifically the SSH connection, a port was forwarded between the client and workspace using:
```
ssh -p 22 -L7001:localhost:7001 <host>
```
where `host` was either an alias for an SSH ProxyCommand that called `coder ssh`, or a Coder Connect hostname.

For latency, [`tcping`](https://www.elifulkerson.com/projects/tcping.php) was used against the forwarded port:
```
tcping -n 100 localhost 7001
```

For throughput, [`iperf3`](https://iperf.fr/iperf-download.php) was used:
```
iperf3 -c localhost -p 7001
```
where an `iperf3` server was running on the workspace on port 7001.

## Test Cases

### Testcase 1: `coder ssh` `ProxyCommand` that bicopies from Coder Connect
This case tests the implementation in this PR, such that we can write a config like:
```
Host codercliconnect
    ProxyCommand /path/to/coder ssh --stdio workspace
```
With Coder Connect enabled, `ssh -p 22 -L7001:localhost:7001 codercliconnect` will use the Coder Connect tunnel. The results were as follows:

**Throughput, 10 tests, back to back:**
- Average throughput across all tests: 788.20 Mbits/sec
- Minimum average throughput: 731 Mbits/sec
- Maximum average throughput: 871 Mbits/sec
- Standard Deviation: 38.88 Mbits/sec

**Latency, 100 RTTs:**
- Average: 0.369ms
- Minimum: 0.290ms
- Maximum: 0.473ms

### Testcase 2: `ssh` dialing Coder Connect directly without a `ProxyCommand`

This is what we assume to be the 'best' way to use Coder Connect

**Throughput, 10 tests, back to back:**
- Average throughput across all tests: 789.50 Mbits/sec
- Minimum average throughput: 708 Mbits/sec
- Maximum average throughput: 839 Mbits/sec
- Standard Deviation: 39.98 Mbits/sec

**Latency, 100 RTTs:**
- Average: 0.369ms
- Minimum: 0.267ms
- Maximum: 0.440ms

### Testcase 3:  `coder ssh` `ProxyCommand` that creates its own Tailnet connection in-process

This is what normally happens when you run `coder ssh`:

**Throughput, 10 tests, back to back:**
- Average throughput across all tests: 610.20 Mbits/sec
- Minimum average throughput: 569 Mbits/sec
- Maximum average throughput: 664 Mbits/sec
- Standard Deviation: 27.29 Mbits/sec

**Latency, 100 RTTs:**
- Average: 0.335ms
- Minimum: 0.262ms
- Maximum: 0.452ms

## Analysis

Performing a two-tailed, unpaired t-test against the throughput of testcases 1 and 2, we find a P value of `0.9450`. This suggests the difference between the data sets is not statistically significant. In other words, there is a 94.5% chance that the difference between the data sets is due to chance.

## Conclusion

From the t-test, and by comparison to the status quo (regular `coder ssh`, which uses gvisor, and is noticeably slower), I think it's safe to say any impact on throughput or latency by the `ProxyCommand` performing a bicopy against Coder Connect is negligible. Users are very much unlikely to run into performance issues as a result of using Coder Connect via `coder ssh`, as implemented in this PR.

Less scientifically, I ran these same tests on my home network with my Sydney workspace, and both throughput and latency were consistent across testcases 1 and 2.

</details>

Each PSL PR needs to have a description, rationale, indication of DNS validation and syntax checking, as well as a number of acknowledgements from the submitter. This template must be included with each PR, and the submitting party MUST provide responses to all of the elements in order to be considered.
-->

<!-- #### READ THIS FIRST ####

If you haven't yet, please read our guidelines:

not get accepted when their submission didn't follow them.

https://github.com/publicsuffix/list/pull/1591, although 
the organization and description were not as substantial 
as desired, which required maintainers time to visit the 
requestor's website to further research.
Having more robust org/desc improves the PR processing 
pace due to the extra cycles not being lost to research.
For an example of what an excellent description in a PR looks like
see https://github.com/publicsuffix/list/pull/615, 
although that example uses an earlier template.
-->

### Checklist of required steps

* [x] Robust Reason for PSL Inclusion

Third-party Limits are used elsewhere, such as at Cloudflare, Let's

the manner in which those third-party systems or products treat 
a given domain name or sub-domains within it.

To be clear, it is appropriate to address how those limits impact 
your domain(s) directly with that third-party, and it is inappropriate 
to submit entries to the PSL as a means to work around those limits or

<!--
The purpose of the question above is to expose limit workarounds.
If there are third party limits that the PR seeks to overcome, those
must be listed within the rationale section of this request, and 
provide a good level of detail the effort that was made to work directly 
with the third part(y|ies) in attempting to address this within their 
rationale response below.
In all cases, software and services should be discouraged from use of
the PSL as a rate-limiting tool, and provide clear instructions to their
own clients, partners and users on the manner in which they can directly

We treat the following as an attestation in the public record of the

-->

<!--

-->

 * [x] The submitter acknowledges that it is their responsibility to maintain the domains within their section. This includes removing names which are no longer used, retaining the _psl DNS entry, and responding to e-mails to the supplied address. Failure to maintain entries may result in removal of individual entries or the entire section.

<!--
The guidelines describe which section to place the entry, what the 
order of commented org placement, order of sorting of entries. 
(hint: TLD then SLD, ascending sorting) Although it seems pedantic, 
the sorting and formatting rules help ensure all of the automation

<!--

author: harmya
body:
### Current
When a user submits:
1. We make call to: `https://tensara.org/api/trpc/problems.createSubmission?batch=1` with
   - Body:
     ```
     code: "code"
     gpuType: "T4"
     language: "cuda"
     problemSlug: "avg-pool-1d"
     ```

2. When successful, second call is made to : `https://tensara.org/api/submissions/direct-submit` with
   - Body:
     ```
     submissionId: "id" (from first response)
     ```
     
This is weird.

### Now 
Using a single endpoint:
- Endpoint: `http://localhost:3000/api/submissions/direct-submit`
- Body: Same payload as originally sent to first endpoint
  ```
  code: "code"
  gpuType: "T4"
  language: "cuda"
  problemSlug: "avg-pool-1d"
  ```
This has reduced complexity, improved latency (fewer round trips) and now we can integrate CLI easily

As discussed amongst maintainers, this PR merges `api` module back as a package.

**Context**

In #1856 (discussion: #1846), the `api` package was split into a separate module to decouple it from openshift-api dependency, which, at that time, was marked as incompatible in our go.mod.
Unfortunately, it caused several issues like inconsistent dependencies (depending on dependabot schedule) and issues with module imports (#1933).
As references to "incompatible" packages have been resolved in #1953, we think it's better to merge the module back as there are no clear benefits left in having it as a separate module (there isn't that much difference in the list of dependencies either).

author: padix-key
body:
Currently the documentations states

> If either the pose or the reference have atoms that are not present in the other, the respective coordinates of these atoms are *NaN*.

This behavior was planned some time ago but never implemented, so it is currently not the case. The original motivation was that the prediction may not contain some atoms that the reference has which would be penalized in a few metrics (currently only affecting the lDDT metrics). 

However such behavior would counteract the case where the reference has expectedly more atoms, as e.g. mentioned [here](https://github.com/aivant/peppr/issues/8#issuecomment-2812870779). Furthermore, this behavior would probably require more effort in each implemented metric, as NaN coordinates need to be properly handled.

For now this PR removes mentions of that behavior. If we decide to implement it at some point, the issue is tracked in #2 .

## Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
Keepalive help prevent database connections from being closed due to inactivity. If a database connection has been silently closed the keepalive packets should cause the socket to realize it and close it before its used.

Turning on keepalive may help solve the intermittent timout exceptions: https://github.com/npgsql/npgsql/issues/4532#issuecomment-1195524918

The tests would sometimes intermittenly fail because of distributedLockException for the IpSecurityRestrictionUpdater. For this reason I also added DisableConcurrentExecution attribute to the IpSecurityResrictionUpdater which seems to have stopped the issue. Made the IpSecurityRestrictionUpdater method a bit more robust.

body:
Disables a conflicting (and identical) mixin when ArchaicFix is installed, and clamps render distance when Angelica or Optifine is missing. Vanilla by itself doesn't check if render distance is in range, so if you install Angelica, crank the render distance above 16, and uninstall Angelica, you'll get runtime crashes until you turn the render distance back down.

Requires https://github.com/embeddedt/ArchaicFix/pull/142

This PR optimizes the orders model by replacing `select *` with explicit column selections in the CTEs. This patch enables Kerberos-secured connections for the Trino engine by:

- Adding logic in TrinoSessionImpl to read these configs and call OkHttpUtil.setupKerberos(...) when enabled.

This allows users to configure Kerberos principal, keytab, credential cache, service name patterns, and credential delegation for Trino connections.

author: juliogt
body:
# Add Kanban-style Candidate Management Endpoints

## Description
This PR adds two new endpoints to support a Kanban-style interface for managing candidates in the recruitment process. The endpoints allow retrieving candidates for a specific position with their current stages and scores, and updating a candidate's interview stage.

## Changes

### New Endpoints
1. `GET /positions/:id/candidates`
   - Retrieves all candidates for a specific position
   - Returns candidate details including:
     - Full name
     - Current interview step
     - Average interview score
     - Application ID

2. `PUT /candidates/:id/stage`
   - Updates a candidate's interview stage
   - Accepts:
     - `interviewStepId` (required)
     - `applicationId` (optional)

### New Files
- `backend/src/application/services/positionService.ts`
- `backend/src/application/services/applicationService.ts`
- `backend/src/presentation/controllers/positionController.ts`
- `backend/src/presentation/controllers/applicationController.ts`
- `backend/src/routes/positionRoutes.ts`
- `backend/src/tests/positionCandidates.test.ts`
- `backend/src/tests/candidateStage.test.ts`
- `backend/src/tests/integration.test.ts`
- `backend/src/tests/setup.ts`
- `prompts/prompts-JJGC.md`

### Modified Files
- `backend/src/index.ts`
  - Added position routes
  - Added conditional server startup for testing
- `backend/src/routes/candidateRoutes.ts`
  - Added new stage update endpoint
- `backend/api-spec.yaml`
  - Added documentation for new endpoints
- `backend/jest.config.js`
  - Added test configuration
  - Added setup file for test environment

### Testing
Added comprehensive test coverage:
- Unit tests for controllers
- Integration tests for API endpoints
- 17 passing tests covering:
  - Successful operations
  - Error handling
  - Input validation
  - Edge cases

## API Documentation

### GET /positions/:id/candidates
```json
[
  {
    "candidateId": 1,
    "fullName": "John Doe",
    "currentInterviewStep": "Technical Interview",
    "averageScore": 8.5,
    "applicationId": 101
  }
]
```

### PUT /candidates/:id/stage
Request:
```json
{
  "interviewStepId": 3,
  "applicationId": 101
}
```

Response:
```json
{
  "message": "Candidate stage updated successfully",
  "data": {
    "candidateId": 1,
    "candidateName": "John Doe",
    "currentStage": "Final Interview",
    "applicationId": 101
  }
}
```

## Testing Instructions
1. Start the server:
   ```bash
   cd backend
   npm run dev
   ```

2. Run the tests:
   ```bash
   npm test
   ```

3. Test the endpoints:
   - GET http://localhost:3010/positions/1/candidates
   - PUT http://localhost:3010/candidates/1/stage

## Notes
- The implementation follows the existing clean architecture pattern
- All database operations are handled through Prisma
- Error handling includes appropriate HTTP status codes and messages
- The server is configured to handle both development and test environments

✨ Implement User Authentication, Task Management, and File Upload with Supabase Integration

## Overview
This PR introduces a comprehensive task management system with user authentication, file upload capabilities, and Supabase integration. The implementation includes a modern, responsive UI with dark mode support and real-time data synchronization.

## Key Features

### 🔐 Authentication System
- Email/Password authentication
- GitHub OAuth integration
- Protected routes and session management
- User profile management
- Secure logout functionality

### 📋 Task Management
- CRUD operations for tasks
- Task categorization (Feature, Bug, Documentation)
- Priority levels (Low, Medium, High)
- Status tracking (Backlog, Todo, In Progress, Done, Canceled)
- Task filtering and search functionality
- Pagination support
- Bulk selection and actions

### 🔄 Data Management

## Technical Details
- Implemented using React with TypeScript
- Supabase for backend services

- React Router for navigation
- Custom UI components

## Testing
- Tested authentication flows

- Validated task management operations
- Checked responsive design across devices
- Confirmed data persistence and synchronization

## Dependencies Added
- @supabase/supabase-js

author: bcijo
body:
## Basic repository structure created

### Datasets
Manages data loading and preprocessing with a standardized format for various tasks.

- **base_dataset.py**: Defines an abstract base class for datasets, inheriting from `torch.utils.data.Dataset`, with methods for initialization, length, and item retrieval.
- **cityscapes.py**: Specific loader for the Cityscapes dataset, handling image and annotation loading and applying transformations.

### Models
Contains base model architectures and task-specific heads for different computer vision tasks.

- **base_model.py**: Base class for models, handling backbone initialization and dynamic attachment of task-specific heads.
- **unet.py**: Implementation of the UNet architecture with a configurable backbone and dynamic head attachment.
- **heads/**: Directory containing modular heads for various tasks, such as semantic segmentation.
  - **semantic_head.py**: Example of a task-specific head for semantic segmentation, outputting per-pixel class predictions.

### Utils
Provides utility functions for data transformations, loss calculations, and performance metrics.

- **transforms.py**: Custom transformations for images and targets, ensuring consistency in augmentations.
- **losses.py**: Task-specific loss functions, supporting features like ignore_index for void labels.
- **metrics.py**: Metrics for evaluating model performance, handling ignore labels during computation.

### Scripts
Includes scripts for training models, evaluating performance, and managing configurations.

- **train.py**: Script to load configurations, datasets, models, and handle the training process with logging and checkpointing.
- **evaluate.py**: Script to load a trained model and evaluate its performance on a test dataset, logging task-specific metrics.
- **setup.py**: Sets up the environment, including random seed initialization, device configuration, and logging setup.
- **config_parser.py**: Loads and validates YAML configuration files, ensuring all required fields are present.

author: pandrex247
body:
## Description
Second PR, follow up to https://github.com/payara/Payara/pull/7305

Removes the `core-aggregator`, `core-bom`, and `core-parent` modules, and reintegrates and aligns the Core modules these managed back into the respective `payara-aggregator`, `payara-nucleus-parent`, and `payara-parent` poms.

Also adds applicable dependencies back into `payara-bom`, and adds the required `${project.version}` dependency version back for those internal dependencies not covered by the `payara-bom`.

I have taken efforts to keep the property and plugin config aligned with where they were before the Core vs. Server split - even when it would be potentially beneficial to move them. The intent is that these will be moved in follow up commits.

Also updates Concurro to 3.1.0-M6, as we're currently using a SNAPSHOT and the reordering of repositories causes an incorrect snapshot version to be retrieved.

Also fixes a couple of pom versions which were still using 6.x.

Additional weirdness and tasks I spotted which I will also look to address separately (if time permits):
* Fix `org.glassfish.hk2:config-generator` - this is a "dead" module, but shouldn't be. Where it currently exists is a cyclic dependency, which we "get around" by not actually using the version in our code and instead pull in an extremely old version published to Maven Central (2.5.0-b53)
* Flashlight module parents - these don't seem to use their own parent module and instead use `nucleus/common`? I assume this is a copy-paste error that occurred at some point, as it's not immediately obvious to me why this is the case
* Remove `production` domain - this is unused in Community
* Misaligned HK2 dependency in `appserver/payara-appserver-modules/jmx-monitoring` - it's using `org.glassfish.hk2:core:2.3.0` instead of `org.glassfish.hk2:hk2-core:3.0.1.payara-p4`
* Remove unused `appserver/admin/runtime` module?
* Remove unused `appserver/registration` module?
* Remove unused `nucleus/cluster/uc`, `nucleus/cluster/windows`, `nucleus/cluster/uc-l10n` modules
  * At the very least, we should exclude `uc-l10n` from the build, as the module it's meant to be localising isn't included!
* ~Remove or reorder MicroProfile repository from `appserver/pom` - its placement has it get pinged first instead of Maven Central, plus I'm not sure we need it anyway~ - now also included
* ~Remove duplicate `payara-nexus-artifacts` repository entry from `nucleus/pom`~ - now also included
* ~Remove duplicate `maven-deploy-config` `<dependencyManagement>` entry in `nucleus/pom`~ - now also included
* Fix Javadoc generation for the distribution - it's broken and just generates an empty jar (it was broken before outside of the Core modules as well)
* Change `deploy.skip` to true except for distributions, which should have `deploy.skip` set to false - tackled [here](https://github.com/payara/Payara/pull/7319)

## Important Info
### Blockers
None

## Testing
### New tests
None

author: theailanguage
body:
Fix subprocess creation errors on Windows for STDIO client connections.
This updates `create_windows_process` to properly handle the case where asyncio cannot create subprocess transports on Windows by falling back to using the `subprocess` module manually.

Additionally, minor import sorting and style issues have been fixed according to `ruff` linter checks.

---

## Motivation and Context

On Windows systems, MCP clients that connect via STDIO were failing with a `NotImplementedError` during `anyio.open_process()`. This is because `asyncio` on Windows does not implement full support for subprocess transports.

This change provides a clean workaround:
- Attempt async process creation first.
- If not supported, fall back to classic `subprocess.Popen` with `asyncio` wrapping.

This allows MCP STDIO clients (e.g., [streamlit_client_ui.py](https://github.com/theailanguage/mcp_client/blob/main/streamlit_client_ui.py)) to work successfully on Windows without changing user workflows.

edit: 
the default event loop comes out as (Windows 11, Python 3.13) - 
<class 'asyncio.windows_events._WindowsSelectorEventLoop'>

My understanding is that https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/555 might work under the ProactorEventLoop, but my patch "might" help to support environments where that’s not the default
- Frameworks like Streamlit, which may run their own event loop internally
- Python 3.13 and above (where SelectorEventLoop is often the default on Windows)
- CI setups or test runners that don’t customize the loop policy
(note - personally I have faced this with my Streamlit UI only)


## How Has This Been Tested?

- Tested manually on Windows 11, Python 3.13.
- Ran [`streamlit_client_ui.py`](https://github.com/theailanguage/mcp_client/blob/main/streamlit_client_ui.py) to launch the MCP client.
- Successfully connected to STDIO MCP servers without errors.
- Validated tool loading and interaction without subprocess creation issues.
- Verified no new `ruff` or `pyright` issues for the updated file.

---

## Breaking Changes

No breaking changes.
- The fallback mechanism is backward compatible.
- Linux/macOS users are unaffected.
- Windows users gain compatibility without needing to change their code.

---


## Types of changes

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [x] Documentation update (style improvements, minor doc updates)

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [MCP Documentation](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
- [x] My code follows the repository's style guidelines
- [x] New and existing tests pass locally
- [x] I have added appropriate error handling
- [x] I have added or updated documentation as needed

## Additional context

This fix is especially important for making MCP tools and agents accessible on all platforms, including Windows, thereby helping broader adoption.

<!--
Thx for you PR :)
Do not forget to read the guidlines: https://github.com/AlbanDAVID/Toutui/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

## Brief summary

- Do not break users config when updating or reinstalling
- Update config if needed when updating Toutui
- Install brew automatically for macOS
- Rephrase comments about dependencies syntax

## Which issue is fixed?

None.

## In-depth Description

<!--
Describe your solution in more depth.
How does it work? Why is this the best solution?
Does it solve a problem that affects multiple users or is this an edge case for your setup?
-->

When installing or updating Toutui, if `$CONFIG_DIR/config.toml` exists, it is merged with `config.example.toml` following these rules:

- for key=value lines (e.g. `address = "localhost"`), if the key is in the user config file, then we keep its value
- common lines, and lines that are only in one of both files, are kept 

Merging is made by section (i.e. it starts merging lines from the `[player]` section, then `[colors]`, ...). It may be overkill, but if variables from different sections have the same name, `hello_toutui.sh` won't confuse them.

With this PR, variables and sections can easily be added in `config.example.toml`, without too much constraint on both dev and users. (hope so)

Also I have added back a line to install brew automatically on macOS if needed. It should work now, but I cannot assert 100%... I have tried it with bash 3.2 tho, and there was no problem calling a child script from hello_toutui.

## How have you tested this?

Tested on archlinux with bash 5.2.37 and bash 3.2

author: tisdall
body:
I went down a bit of a rabbit hole on this one...

I started off looking at `urllib3` and noticing that while the changelog says `>=2.2.3` I'm actually locked to `2.2.2` in my production environment.  This is because the CI tests are run using `requirements.txt` but anyone using this package uses the requirements in `setup.py`.  Then I noticed there's more discrepancies...   You have a `requirements-test.txt` but it's not actually used at all for the CI, the `requirements.txt` has other discrepancies from what's quoted in `setup.py`, `setup.py` is using `test_require` and `test_suite` but neither actually exist any more in `setuptools` ...

I didn't want to spend too much time on this, so ended up with this change to limit how much I'm rewriting.  This PR puts all the requirements in a single place in `setup.py`.  However, developments in python packaging mean these things should really be in `setup.cfg` (you'll get a warning about it if you run the README suggested `python setup.py develop`).

author: its-define
body:
## Pull Request: Add Livepeer LLM Inference Plugin to Eliza Framework

### Description
This PR introduces the **Livepeer LLM Inference Plugin** for the Eliza framework. It enables language-model inference via Livepeer’s API gateway, allowing agents to leverage a variety of models without requiring individual API keys.

---

### Features
- **LLM Inference Processing**  
  Seamless POST requests to Livepeer’s `/llm` endpoint for chat-style interactions.
- **Multi-Model Support**  
  Automatically selects from small or large models, or custom endpoints, based on configuration.
- **Zero-Key Integration**  
  No need for proprietary API keys—uses gateway defaults or runtime settings.

---

### Implementation Details
- **New Package**  
  Added `packages/plugin-livepeer-inference/` containing the TypeScript plugin and Zod schema.
- **Config Schema**  
  Validates and parses:  
  - `LIVEPEER_GATEWAY_URL`  
  - Optional model overrides (`LIVEPEER_MODEL`, `LIVEPEER_LARGE_MODEL`)  
  - Runtime overrides for `temperature` and `maxTokens`
- **Core Logic**  
  - `callLivepeerLLM()` helper builds messages and handles HTTP calls  
  - Exposes three hooks under `ModelType`:  
    - `TEXT_SMALL`  
    - `TEXT_LARGE`  
    - `TEXT_EMBEDDING` (character-code embedding fallback)

---

### Setup & Usage
1. **Install**  
   ```bash
   pnpm install packages/plugin-livepeer-inference
   ```
2. **Configure**  
   - Add your gateway URL in `.env` or runtime settings:  
     ```env
     LIVEPEER_GATEWAY_URL=https://your-gateway.livepeer.com
     LIVEPEER_MODEL=meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
     ```
   - (Optional) Override temperature or max tokens:  
     ```env
     LIVEPEER_TEMPERATURE=0.7
     LIVEPEER_MAX_TOKENS=1024
     ```
3. **Enable**  
   Include `"plugin-livepeer-inference"` in your agent’s `plugins` array.

---

### Testing
- **Test Suite**:  
  - Core inference flows covered under `packages/plugin-livepeer-inference/tests/*`  
  - Zod schema validation tests for missing/invalid config
- **Integration**:  
  Verified against [[UD1sto/elizav2-livepeer](https://github.com/UD1sto/elizav2-livepeer)](https://github.com/UD1sto/elizav2-livepeer)
- **Known Issue**:  
  - Intermittent `503 Gateway` errors on reflection LLM calls from the bootstrap plugin. Under investigation; core flow still completes successfully.

---

### Checklist
- [x] Added TypeScript typings and Zod schema  
- [x] Wrote unit tests covering main code paths  
- [x] Verified end-to-end flow in demo repository  
- [ ] Resolve 503 error

author: glenn-syj
body:
# Implement Writer Pattern for Immutable Segments

## Overview
Refactored segment file handling to implement writer pattern, ensuring immutability and thread safety. This resolves the critical design issues identified in #3.

## Key Changes

### 1. Writer Pattern Implementation
- Added `SegmentFileWriter` abstract class
- Implemented type-specific writers (`DocumentFileWriter`, `DictionaryFileWriter`, `PostingFileWriter`, `MetaFileWriter`)
- Separated file creation and reading operations
- Enforced immutability after file completion

### 2. Storage Interface Enhancement
- Deprecated direct file creation methods
- Added writer-based creation methods
- Improved file type validation
- Enhanced error handling and messages

### 3. File Management
- Implemented read-only file access
- Added proper file extension handling
- Improved resource cleanup
- Enhanced buffer management

### 4. Dictionary File Structure Enhancement
- Added metadata section after header:
  ```
  [Header]
  [Metadata]
    - termRecordsPosition (long)
    - termIndexPosition (long)
    - blockCount (int)
  [Term Records]
  [Term Index]
  ```
- Improved term lookup performance
- Better memory management for large dictionaries
- Cleaner separation between reading and writing operations

## Test Coverage
All tests have been updated to use the new writer pattern:
```language=java
// Before: Direct file modification
SegmentFile file = storage.createFile("test", FileType.DOC);
// ... modify file ...

// After: Writer pattern
DocumentFileWriter writer = storage.createFileWriter("test", FileType.DOC);
// ... write content ...
SegmentFile file = writer.complete();
```

## Migration Guide
1. Replace direct file creation with appropriate writer
2. Use writer methods for content creation
3. Call `complete()` to finalize and get read-only file
4. Remove any file modification after creation

Closes #3

author: callein
body:
## 주요 변경사항
-	태그 할당(Tag Assignment)이 성공한 후, 해당 주제(Subject)의 is_tag_assigned 필드를 true로 업데이트하는 로직을 추가했습니다.
-	client.update_is_tag_assigned_true(subjectId) 호출을 통해 외부 API를 호출하여 상태를 반영합니다.
-	이를 위해 헬퍼 메서드 update_subject_tag_assignment(client, assign_resp_dtos_list)를 새롭게 작성했습니다.
-	크론 스크립트에서 신규/재시도 작업(process_feeds_with_date, process_failed_feeds) 모두 완료 후 업데이트가 진행됩니다.
-	HandongFeedAppClient.update_is_tag_assigned_true 메서드에 예외 처리를 개선했습니다.  
	- requests 라이브러리 import를 메서드 내부가 아닌 모듈 최상단으로 이동했습니다.
	- 예외 발생 시 from e 문법을 적용하여 예외 체이닝을 명확히 했습니다.
	- GET, POST 메서드에도 패치와 동일한 레벨의 상세한 에러 로깅을 추가했습니다.
- 	`BaseAPIClient` 클래스에서 get, post, patch 메서드에 중복되던 HTTP 요청 및 예외 처리 로직을 하나의 private 메서드 `_send_request`로 통합했습니다.
	-	각 HTTP 메서드(get, post, patch)는 `_send_request`를 호출하여 코드 중복 없이 간결하게 구현되었습니다.

## 추가 설명
-	태그가 성공적으로 할당된 경우에만 is_tag_assigned를 true로 변경합니다.
-	Subject Id가 없는 경우에는 예외를 발생시키지 않고, 정상적인 흐름만 처리합니다.
-	헬퍼 메서드를 통해 중복 코드를 제거하고, 로직의 재사용성과 가독성을 높였습니다.
- API 호출 시 204 No Content 정상 응답을 기대하고, 404/403 등 에러 응답에 대해 명확하게 예외를 발생시킵니다.

## 관련 작업
-	HandongFeedApp 내 /api/external/subject/{subjectId}/tag-assigned PATCH API 호출
-	update_is_tag_assigned_true 호출 시 204 No Content 정상 응답을 기대

>  The <update_contact/> tag is an optional tag which can be added to provide an email address distributors can use to contact the project about invalid or incomplete metadata or – in case the specification has changed – about old metadata. It can also be used to ask general questions in case of an update of the component described in the metadata file.
The <update_contact/> tag must only be used by distributors. It is not included in the distribution-provided AppStream XML file, and therefore not exposed to the end user via any kind of UI.
Upstream authors might decide to add an email address in cleartext, but spam protection using _AT_ is also valid. The value of this tag is generally treated a case-insensitive way.

body:
- **Decoupled GuildPlayer initialization:** The initialization logic for `GuildPlayer` is now separated. Instead of being created directly in `NewGuildPlayer`, `PlaybackController` and `PlaylistManager` are instantiated separately.
    - **Purpose:** Improves modularity and testability of the `GuildPlayer` component.
    - **Technical Impact:**  Reduces the complexity of the `NewGuildPlayer` function and allows for easier mocking of dependencies in tests.

- **Introduced `PlaybackHandler` and `PlaylistHandler` interfaces:** New interfaces `PlaybackHandler` and `PlaylistHandler` are added which are implemented by `PlaybackController` and `PlaylistManager` respectively.
    - **Purpose:**  Defines clear contracts for playback and playlist management, enabling future implementations or variations.
    - **Technical Impact:** Increases flexibility and promotes the principle of dependency inversion.

- **Refactored `Config` struct:** The `Config` struct now includes `PlaybackHandler` and `PlaylistHandler` dependencies.
    - **Purpose:**  Provides necessary dependencies for the `GuildPlayer` during initialization.
    - **Technical Impact:** Aligns the configuration with the new handler interfaces.

body:
This PR addresses issues encountered when running drawrnajs, specifically errors such as `getCoordsNAVIEW is undefined`. The root causes were related to incorrect export patterns and method scoping in the NAView layout modules. These changes ensure that both `getCoordsNAVIEW` and `NAView` are correctly defined, scoped, and exported. This eliminates reference errors and allows drawrnajs to initialize and run without crashing.

### Changes made
- **`src/layouts/naview/getnaview.js`**  
  - Refactored `getCoordsNAVIEW` to be properly defined as a function before exporting.  
  - Moved the `module.exports = getCoordsNAVIEW` statement to the end of the file after the function declaration.
  
- **`src/layouts/naview/naview.js`**  
  - Refactored `NAView` from being directly assigned to `module.exports` to a standard function declaration.  
  - Fixed scoping issues where `determine_depths` was previously defined as a standalone function; it is now correctly set as a method on `NAView.prototype` and called with `this.determine_depths()`.
  - Added `module.exports = NAView` at the end of the file to properly export the constructor function.

author: codegen-sh[bot]
body:
This PR updates the RatauraAgent to use different LLM models depending on whether voice is enabled or not, as requested.

## Changes:

- Modified the RatauraAgent class to use different LLM models based on the `voice_enabled` setting:
  - When voice is enabled: Uses the Gemini multimodal `RealtimeModel` for real-time voice processing
  - When voice is disabled (text-only mode): Uses the standard LLM model from `settings.llm_provider()`

## Implementation Details:

The agent now conditionally selects the appropriate LLM model during initialization:
- For voice mode, it continues to use the Gemini multimodal `RealtimeModel` with silero VAD
- For text-only mode, it uses the standard LLM model defined in the config's `llm_provider` method

This implementation ensures that the agent uses the most appropriate model for each mode:
- The real-time model for voice interactions
- The standard model for text-only interactions

All existing functionality is preserved, including the environment variable toggle for switching between modes.

author: sterlinghofmann
body:
This commit introduces a new example demonstrating the usage of hardware interrupts on the Xiao BLE Sense board. The example includes GPIO interrupts for handling button presses and provides a simple application for developers to understand how to configure and handle interrupts on this board.

While a GPIO interrupt example exists under `samples/basic/button`, this implementation is tailored to the specific setup of the Xiao BLE Sense board, providing clarity for developers who may struggle with understanding the configuration process for setting up interrupts. This example aims to reduce setup complexity for future developers working with hardware interrupts on this board.

Additionally, more interrupt examples (e.g., data-ready and inactivity interrupts) can be added later if the community finds them valuable, as they require different registers to be active.

- Created a new folder `samples/boards/seeed/xiao_ble_sense/hardware_interrupt`.
- Added `main.c` demonstrating basic GPIO interrupt handling.
- Added a .overlay file showing how to configure the INT1 pin.
- Updated README with usage instructions for the example.
